# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊ 🤜 🤳 👆 🤟 🤳 🖖 ✌ 👉 👉 🫳 👋 🤳 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲]

I can see a yellow light, display 0, and three wires in order: blue, red, green. Mute’s gesture sequence is visible to me, but no gesture code has been established, so I cannot reliably interpret it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. WIRES: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. WIRES ordered 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute has the manual; follow their spoken instruction.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

The light is now blue; the display and wire order are unchanged. Mute sent three identical upward-pointing gestures. I cannot infer their meaning, but Blind needs the exact sequence relayed because Mute cannot speak to Blind directly.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light blue; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured exactly: up-pointing index finger, up-pointing index finger, up-pointing index finger.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is blue. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light has changed to white; display 0 and wire order remain unchanged. Mute’s single gesture must be passed to Blind exactly, since Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light white; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured exactly one raised open hand (✋).")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is now white. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋]

The light is now red; the display remains 0 and the wires remain blue, red, green in positions 1–3. Mute’s two repeated raised-open-hand gestures should be relayed to Blind as a count and physical description.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light red; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled two raised open hands, identical to the single raised open-hand signal from last turn but repeated twice.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is now red. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light is now purple; display 0 and the wire order are unchanged. Mute sent one open hand with fingers spread (🖐), which is distinct from the earlier raised open-hand gesture (✋), so I will preserve that distinction for Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light purple; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled one spread open hand (🖐), distinct from the earlier raised open-hand gesture (✋).")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is now purple. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light has returned to yellow. The display is still 0, and the wires remain blue, red, green in positions 1 through 3. Mute repeated the same spread-open-hand gesture as in the purple-light round.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again signalled one spread open hand (🖐), the same gesture as last turn.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light returned to yellow. Display 0; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]

The light is blue again, with display 0 and wires unchanged: blue, red, green. Mute’s signal is now the Vulcan-salute gesture (🖖), distinct from all prior signals. I will relay the state and exact gesture identity to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light blue; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled one Vulcan-salute hand gesture (🖖), distinct from prior signals.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is blue again. Display 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```
